Receive requests for physical octree nodes from the ray-caster [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the ray-caster detects cache misses of virtual octree nodes required for traversal. When a cache miss occurs and cannot be satisfied by the CPU cache, the system reconstructs physical data. The text describes a 'demand-driven data back-end' that runs in a separate background thread. The mechanism described is that the ray-caster identifies the need for specific data (via cache misses) and triggers the reconstruction process. Therefore, the ray-caster effectively 'receives' or generates the request for physical data (by triggering the back-end via cache miss detection) to satisfy the rendering needs. The claim that it 'receives requests for physical octree nodes' is supported by the description of the ray-caster driving data reconstruction by detecting these misses and the back-end responding to these needs.
